maya: Heads up — canary deploy for r2 runtime showing a 35% p99 spike and a compile-worker backlog after today's merge. p99 went 120ms -> 165ms, tokens/sec down ~18%.
aj: Seeing the same in us-west-2-a, service=runtime-v2. Traces show a lot of JIT/compile churn at request spikes.
diego: perf-bot already raised a CI alert earlier: runtime-e2e-perf failed with a 22% regression on the perf job. Link: https://perf.internal/jobs/1762500500
perf-bot: Alert: perf/regressions: runtime-e2e-perf @1762500500 - p99 +22% vs baseline. Artifact: perf-trace-1762500500
selena: Starting a bisect now. Suspected commit range 6a3f..b7e2 from the release notes; will run kernel selector bench locally.
maya: Quick local profiling shows kernel autopicker picked "matmul_8x8_tile" for fp16 seq=128 on A100, whereas previously we used "matmul_16x4_tile" which was faster for our pattern. Also observing KV cache invalidations coincident with compilations (TTL resets). Snippet:
```
[kernel-selector] Selected kernel: matmul_8x8_tile (score=0.42)
[kernel-selector] Candidate: matmul_16x4_tile (score=0.38)
[compile-worker] enqueue_compile job=matmul_8x8_tile id=0x7f2
[kv-cache] invalidate prefix=session-abc ttl=30 -> new-ttl=0 (reset after compile)
```
aj: That looks like the scoring changes from the latest selector tweak. PR #4821 changed score normalization and warmup penalties.
diego: Bisect result: culprit is commit b7e2f9c "kernel-selector: normalize-scores". Reverting that commit locally restores previous kernel picks and fixes throughput.
selena: We should block the rollout and revert in prod-canary. Can someone hit the release hold?
release-bot: Hold placed on rollout r2-runtime. Reason: performance regression detected (p99 +35% on canary). Tracking ticket INF-1284.
sre-oncall: I'll spin up extra compile-workers to drain the queue and temporarily increase KV cache TTL to reduce invalidations while we revert.
maya: Immediate mitigations: set KVCACHE_TTL=300 and disable dynamic kernel-weight updates (KERNEL_WEIGHTS=stable) in canary config. Preparing revert PR now.
aj: Pushed revert branch r2-revert-kernel-normalization and triggered perf CI. Also added a short- lived feature flag to avoid dynamic normalization in canary.
perf-bot: Perf run complete: runtime-e2e-perf @1762501700 - p99 +2% vs baseline. Regression resolved.
diego: Follow-up items: add a unit test that fails if normalization can flip preferences for tile-size in known microbenchmarks. Filing INF-1285.
selena: Also proposing a CI gate: abort rollouts if compile queue depth > 10 sustained for 5m (compile-storm detector). Will file INF-1286.
maya: Thanks all — will coordinate canary rollback and the postmortem. :thumbsup:
aj: Leaving a note for the postmortem and linking perf traces + bisect commands used.
